item.title: NASA rushed engineers out of their labs. They say it risks future space missions
item.description: NASA employees say they've lost vital equipment and staff needed to make sophisticated spacecraft amid the agency's abrupt relocations over the past several months.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Trump's EPA repeals pollution limits on fossil fuel power plants
item.description: The Trump administration is eliminating limits on climate-warming pollution from the nation's fossil fuel power plants. Environmental groups say this will impact the climate and public health.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: New Carlo Rovelli book challenges science's understanding of reality and the universe
item.description: In his latest book, the world-renowned physicist draws on science and philosophy to explore the notion that the university and reality are fully knowable.

item.title: Pennsylvania says an unvaccinated woman has died from measles-related complications
item.description: Pennsylvania has announced its third measles-related death in less than three weeks. A local coroner says the 40-year-old woman was unvaccinated.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Actor Tatyana Ali is advocating for Black and Indigenous maternal health
item.description: Actor Tatyana Ali says her healing journey after a traumatic childbirth has inspired her advocacy for Black maternal health, including support for midwives, doulas and other birth workers.

item.title: This summer was hot. August shattered global heat records
item.description: Scientists say that August was the hottest month ever recorded globally. In the U.S., summer temperatures also shattered heat records.

item.title: A fossil feather from the age of dinosaurs may explain why only some birds survived
item.description: An extremely well preserved fossil feather could reveal why some birds survived the dinosaur-killing asteroid, and others did not.

item.title: Scientists say August was Earth's hottest month they've measured
item.description: The European climate service Copernicus said the Earth just sweltered through its hottest month on record in August. Scientists said the heat surge is mostly due to human-caused climate change.
item.content:encoded:

item.title: Are we any closer to detecting dark matter?
item.description: NPR's Scott Detrow talks with theoretical astrophysicist Priyamvada Natarajan of Yale University about a strange blip recorded by a dark matter detector in South Dakota and what the fluke could mean.

item.title: 'Her body temperature was 106': How heat is killing Americans in their homes
item.description: Heat kills thousands of people across the U.S. every year. The risk is especially high for the millions of Americans who live in manufactured housing like mobile homes and trailers.
